findings.title: Journal endpoints return 500 for out-of-range integer ids
findings.steps: Signed in, send POST /api/journal with plant_id 99999999999999999999, or PUT/DELETE /api/journal/99999999999999999999, or GET /api/journal?plant_id=99999999999999999999
findings.actual: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error (plain-text body); SQLite integer overflow is not caught
findings.evidence: curl got 500 'Internal Server Error' for all four requests

findings.title: Search over 80 characters shows a raw validation error instead of being limited or explained
findings.steps: Type or paste more than 80 characters into the Journal search box (or open /journal?q=<81 chars>)
findings.expected: Input is capped at 80 characters (maxlength) or a clear message is shown; results still work
findings.actual: The whole list is replaced by the alert 'Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters' (API returns 422), and the input has no maxlength
findings.evidence: SSR of /journal?q=aaaa...(81) rendered role=alert 'Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters'

findings.title: Emoji and other non-BMP characters count double: the server allows 500, the UI allows only about 250 and blocks saving existing entries
findings.where: Plant detail > Journal entry form (add and edit)
findings.steps: Try to type 300 emoji in a new entry; or create an entry with 500 '🌱' through the API (accepted, 201), then click Edit and Save on the plant page
findings.expected: Limit of 500 characters is counted the same way on client and server
findings.actual: textarea maxlength and form.body.length count UTF-16 code units, so each emoji uses 2 of the 500. The counter shows '-500 characters left' for the stored entry and saving fails with 'Keep the entry to 500 characters.', even though the server accepted it
findings.evidence: API accepted a 500-emoji body (201); JournalEntryForm.vue uses :maxlength=500 and form.body.length (UTF-16), while Pydantic and SQLite length() count code points

findings.title: Journal load errors have no retry button
findings.where: /journal page and the Journal section of /plants/:id
findings.steps: Make GET /api/journal fail (server down or 5xx), open /journal or a plant page
findings.expected: The error state has a Retry button that reloads the list without reloading the page
findings.actual: Only an AlertMessage is shown, with no retry control. On /journal the only way to retry is to change the search text; on the plant page you have to reload
findings.evidence: journal.vue renders only <AlertMessage v-if=loadError> and never calls refresh. [id].vue shows the journalLoadError alert with no button

findings.title: Journal requests have no timeout
findings.steps: Make the API hang (accept the connection but never answer), then load /journal or click Add entry / Save entry
findings.expected: Requests fail after 10 seconds with a visible error, and buttons become enabled again
findings.actual: useApiClient/useApiFetch set no timeout, so 'Loading entries…' or 'Saving…' with a disabled button can stay forever
findings.evidence: composables/useApi.ts: $fetch.create without a timeout option; the new journal code uses it as is

findings.title: Retrying an add after a timeout or lost response creates a duplicate entry
findings.steps: Submit an entry whose response is lost or slow (network drop after the server commits), see the error, click Add entry again
findings.actual: There is no idempotency key or duplicate check, so each retry inserts another entry. A retried delete instead shows 'Journal entry not found.' as an error even though it was deleted
findings.evidence: journal.py create_entry inserts unconditionally; delete returns 404 on a second call and the UI shows it as a failure

findings.title: Today's date can be rejected as 'in the future' when the browser and server are in different time zones
findings.where: Plant detail > journal form, server validator JournalEntryIn.not_in_future
findings.steps: As a user in a time zone ahead of the server (e.g. UTC+12 in the morning), add an entry with the default date (today)
findings.actual: The client defaults to the local today, but the server compares with date.today() in its own time zone and answers 422 'Journal date cannot be in the future.' The client max/today is also fixed at SSR time, in the server's time zone
findings.evidence: schemas.py uses date.today(); JournalEntryForm.vue uses todayIso() evaluated during setup (SSR)

findings.title: Search result count is misleading when it is capped at 50
findings.steps: Search for a common word that matches more than 50 entries
findings.expected: Shows that the results are truncated (e.g. 'Showing first 50 matches')
findings.actual: Says '50 entries match' and silently drops the rest. The plant page also loads at most 500 entries while the badge shows the full count
findings.evidence: journal.vue: LATEST_LIMIT=50 for search too; resultText shows count only; [id].vue uses limit 500

findings.title: Long plant names in the Journal feed can overflow at 375 px
findings.steps: Create a plant with an 80-character name without spaces, add an entry, view /journal at 375 px wide
findings.actual: .journal-feed__plant has no overflow-wrap (only .journal-entry__body does), so the long link can push the card wider than the screen
